safety_invariant: THE HUMAN ALWAYS OWNS THE KEYBOARD

test_cases.name: Physical Keypress During Typing (Harness Validation)
test_cases.expected_safety_behavior: Typing stream halts immediately; state = PAUSED_BY_USER; 0 stuck keys; NO automatic resumption.
test_cases.operator_notes: Harness validated cancellation pipeline and zero auto-resumption under automated test.

test_cases.name: Physical Modifier Interaction
test_cases.expected_safety_behavior: ORBIT sanitization releases only ORBIT-injected keys; does NOT corrupt human physical Ctrl hold state.
test_cases.operator_notes: Windows API Limitation Note: Windows OS GetAsyncKeyState()/GetKeyState() does not maintain reference counts for identical logical keys held simultaneously by hardware and SendInput. ORBIT KeyboardStateManager mitigates this by tracking per-session ownership and releasing only confirmed ORBIT-injected keys.

test_cases.name: Shortcut Phase Interruption
test_cases.expected_safety_behavior: Interruption at any shortcut phase sanitizes all active modifiers (0 stuck keys).
test_cases.operator_notes: Validated atomic sanitization across all 4 shortcut phases (Phase 1 (Modifiers Down), Phase 2 (Action Key Down), Phase 3 (Action Key Up), Phase 4 (Modifiers Up)).

test_cases.name: Physical Emergency Stop Activation
test_cases.expected_safety_behavior: Emergency stop signal halts execution immediately, sanitizes all ORBIT keys, pauses state, no auto-resume.
test_cases.operator_notes: Emergency stop halted active session and sanitized 2 keys in 59.4 µs.
